location: projects list — project card subtitle/faction text (e.g. .faction 'Orks', 'Adeptus Astartes'); same dim token used for card meta
problem: Faction/subtitle text is rgb(90,103,114) #5A6772 on background #050607, measured 3.49:1 at 11px regular. Fails AA normal-text minimum of 4.5:1. This is the secondary identifying line on every project card, so it fails app-wide.
fix: Lighten the dim text token from #5A6772 to at least #8A98A6 (~4.7:1 on #050607) — or reuse the existing #98A2AD token already used elsewhere (7.83:1). One CSS custom property change applied to the faction/meta class.

principle: Refactoring UI — Hierarchy (the most important element must not be the one that gets sacrificed); WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow
location: projects list — project card grid (.card name column vs palette+progress columns) at <= ~900px
problem: At tablet (768px) the project NAME — the primary identifier — truncates to 'Ork B…' / 'Tactic…' while the decorative 5-dot palette and the fixed-width ASCII progress bar keep their full width. The most important data is the first thing dropped. Card layout squeezes the name column instead of reflowing.
fix: Below ~900px, drop the palette dots and the inline ASCII progress bar first (mobile already does this) and give the name column flex:1 with no truncation, or wrap the name to a second line. Reserve truncation for the name only as a last resort and add title attribute. Trigger the existing mobile card layout at the md breakpoint, not just sm.

principle: Refactoring UI — Hierarchy; Apple HIG Clarity
location: projects list — sub-project / detail-page child rows; project name truncates even at 1440px
problem: On the detail page the sub-project row shows 'Tactical Squad A…' truncated even at full 1440px desktop width, because the palette+progress+status columns reserve fixed width regardless of available space. Truncating a 20-char name on a 1440px screen is needless and signals a brittle fixed-pixel layout.
fix: Make the name column flex-grow and let the right-hand status cluster shrink-to-content rather than reserving fixed width; the ASCII progress bar can use a shorter cell count (e.g. 11 chars) and still leave room. Verify 'Tactical Squad Alpha' renders in full at >=1024px.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency & Standards; Refactoring UI — Color (one semantic = one value)
location: project detail — aggregated stage bars (#1EA845) vs project/sub-project row progress bars (#33FF66)
problem: Two different greens are used for the identical 'filled progress' meaning: aggregated stage counters render the filled blocks in rgb(30,168,69) #1EA845 while the unit/header progress bars use rgb(51,255,102) #33FF66. Same semantic, two colors — reads as accidental rather than intentional and weakens the visual system.
fix: Standardise the 'progress fill' on a single token. Recommend #33FF66 (the §9 phosphor-green reference) for all completed-progress fills; if the dimmer green is intentional for aggregated/read-only data, document it as a distinct token and apply it consistently to every read-only bar.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of System Status; NN/g #5 Error Prevention; Material 3 disabled-state guidance
location: project detail — '[ edit ]' control top-right of header (span, aria-disabled=true, cursor:not-allowed)
problem: The '[ edit ]' control is correctly aria-disabled with cursor:not-allowed, but visually it is rendered in the exact dim color (#5A6772, 3.49:1) used for normal secondary text. A sighted user cannot distinguish 'disabled / coming soon' from 'an active but quiet link', so clicking it produces nothing with no explanation. It sits exactly where an active edit affordance is expected.
fix: Either (a) hide the edit control entirely until the feature ships, or (b) give the disabled state an unmistakable visual: append a '(soon)' label, reduce opacity to ~0.4 against a clearly-different treatment, and surface a tooltip/visible note on hover. Do not rely on cursor:not-allowed alone — it is invisible until hover.

principle: NN/g #8 Aesthetic & Minimalist Design; Refactoring UI — design for real data
location: projects list — 'Ork Boyz Mob' appears in both 'Backlog' section and 'All projects' section
problem: The same project row ('Ork Boyz Mob', same /projects/4vTUVDim9EsCO1ah link) renders twice on one screen — once under Backlog and again under All projects. With only 2-3 visible items the duplication is conspicuous and makes the count ('1 unit waiting' vs the same row below) feel redundant. As the list grows, 'All projects' duplicating everything already shown in Backlog/Active doubles scroll length.
fix: Decide the section model: either (a) 'All projects' excludes items already surfaced in Backlog/Active, or (b) drop the curated Backlog/Active sections in favour of a single grouped/filterable list. If the dual presentation is intentional, visually de-emphasise the 'All projects' repeat or label it 'Everything (incl. above)'.

principle: Refactoring UI — design for real content; Apple HIG Clarity (no truncation of labels)
location: projects list — quick-add input (placeholder 'e.g. "Necron Warriors x20" or "Sergeant Vraks"') top-right toolbar
problem: The quick-add input is a fixed ~333px wide and its placeholder is clipped mid-word ('...or "Sergea') at desktop, tablet AND mobile. The example never reads as a complete thought, so the affordance's purpose (free-text quick capture) is half-communicated. The cramped top-right placement also competes with the '[ + ] New project' link directly below it.
fix: Either shorten the placeholder to one example that fits ('e.g. Necron Warriors x20') or let the input grow to fill available header width (flex:1, min-width:0). On mobile, move quick-add to full width below the heading rather than the cramped inline slot.

location: projects list — quick-add submit button (renders as '+', disabled until input)
problem: The quick-add submit button has no accessible name other than its visible '+' glyph and no aria-label/title, so a screen reader announces only 'plus, button'. Its purpose (add the typed project) is not programmatically clear.
fix: Add aria-label="Add project" (or title) to the '+' submit button. Trivial attribute addition.

principle: Apple HIG / Material 3 touch-target 44x44 (note: passes WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 24px floor)
location: projects list — quick-add '+' submit button (32x32px); sidebar nav links (36px tall); logo link (19px tall)
problem: The '+' submit button is 32x32px and desktop sidebar nav links are 36px tall — below the 44x44 Apple/Material comfortable-target guideline (they DO clear the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum, so this is polish, not a legal failure). The 'MINI MANAGER' logo link is only 19px tall. Mobile bottom-nav targets are a healthy 56px, so this is desktop/tablet only.
fix: Pad the '+' submit button to 44x44 (it has room next to a 37px input). Increase desktop nav row height to 44px (currently 36) and the logo link tap area to ~44px. Spacing-scale change, no layout restructure.

principle: Vintage Terminal/CRT §9 — 'Use #0D0D0D not #000000 as background' (halation on OLED / astigmatism)
problem: The page background is #050607, darker than the §9-recommended #0D0D0D-#111111 floor. Near-pure black plus the bright #33FF66/#00E5FF phosphor text and glow maximises halation (the bright-on-black halo effect) for users with astigmatism and bloom on OLED. The aesthetic is otherwise well-judged; this is the one value that pushes past the guideline.
fix: Raise the base background from #050607 to #0D0D0D (and card surfaces to #111111-#161616). Single token change at :root; preserves the terminal look while reducing halation.

location: project detail — 'Attach recipe' and 'Shopping for this' exposed in the heading hierarchy alongside true section headings; 'Attach recipe' surfaces as an h2
problem: The accessibility tree shows 'Attach recipe' as an <h2>, sitting in the heading outline next to genuine section headings ('Recipe', 'Sub-projects', 'Aggregated stages'). 'Attach recipe' is an action, not a section, so it pollutes the screen-reader heading navigation. Heading order is otherwise clean (h1 then h2s, no skips).
fix: Render the 'Attach recipe' / quick-action labels as button text, not as heading elements. Keep only true section titles as <h2>. Confirm the heading outline reads: Project name (h1) > Sub-projects, Aggregated stages, Recipe, Shopping for this (h2).

principle: NN/g #8 Aesthetic & Minimalist Design (polish); branding completeness
location: global — /favicon.ico returns 404 on both prod (miniaturemanager.vercel.app) and local
problem: The only console error on every page is a 404 for /favicon.ico. No favicon means a blank/default tab icon in the browser and a recurring console error — a small but visible polish gap, especially for an app meant to be 'carried in your pocket at the hobby store' (PWA/home-screen feel).
fix: Add an app icon: place favicon.ico plus apple-touch-icon and a Next.js app/icon.(png|svg) in src/app/. A terminal-green box-drawing or 'MM' mark fits the aesthetic. Resolves the 404 and gives the tab/home-screen an identity.
